findings: G-001: mandatory previous / next → 上一页 / 下一页 is an over-constraint / cross-surface semantic collision. Unified corpus uses previous/next broadly in learn-docs-v1 for previous versions, previous step, next operation, next result set, next scheduled minor releases, etc.; the unqualified global mandatory rule incorrectly extends Tour navigation semantics across surfaces.

G-002: keep Shift is an invalid keep / lexical identity collision. In the Tour eligible Example teaching comment 'Shift it right again 99 places...' Shift is an ordinary English verb, not a keyboard-key identity; an unqualified global keep would force legitimate natural-language English residue.

G-003: keep Enter is an invalid keep / current-source contradiction. Current Unified Corpus contains UI source 'Enter the tour', where Enter is an ordinary UI verb, not the Enter-key identity; the bare global keep conflicts with translatable current source.

G-004: generic / generics lacks a unified terminology decision. The terms occur across Tour and Learn/Docs in high-impact generics article/SEO/module/tutorial contexts; the versionless glossary must make an explicit consistent terminology decision for this core cross-surface concept.
